note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The claim is that a subring containing every graded projector inherits the homogeneous decomposition of the endomorphism ring. A proof has to use the finiteness of the grading to ensure that the displayed sums remain algebraic sums inside the subring, and then check multiplication of the components.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:3 — reading question
note_matches.text: The small insertion specifying which module underlies the endomorphism ring is difficult to resolve, and the square bracket opened in the main paragraph has no confidently identified closing partner on this sheet. The correction from algebra language to subring language should be retained as a revision rather than silently harmonised.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:4:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Orthogonal idempotents summing to one are asserted to induce the required homogeneous decomposition. The subsequent block decomposition supplies a proof strategy; the marginal extension from ℤ to an arbitrary group would require careful attention to the order of multiplication for a noncommutative grading group.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:6:4 — unpursued implication

note_matches.text: The claim is that a subring containing every graded projector inherits the homogeneous decomposition of the endomorphism ring. note_matches.heading: ## Fourier transforms, determinant lines, and Chern coefficients
note_matches.text: These post-freeze notes concern cote 47, scans 3–11; this file is undated, so the comparisons below make no claim of historical priority. Manuscript assertions, established literature, and editorial calculations are identified separately, and none changes the frozen transcription. In explanatory formulas only, write \(B=A^\vee\), \(g=n\), \(\pi_A:A\to S\), \(P\) for the Poincaré bundle rigidified along both zero sections, \(\omega_A=\det(\operatorname{Lie}A)^\vee\) on \(S\), and \(\tau_A=\omega_A^{-1}\); pullbacks of base classes are displayed or understood from their destination.

note_matches.heading: ### F4 — Cote 47, scan 5, inserted determinant factor; scans 6–7, Lemma 1
note_matches.text: Dualizing the Hodge-line identification gives \(\det\operatorname{Lie}A\simeq\det\operatorname{Lie}B\), without a principal polarization or an identification of the full Lie bundles. His Lemma 1.2.5 also identifies the Poincaré direct image with the zero-section pushforward of this inverse Hodge line, shifted by \(-g\); this preserves canonicity without choosing a trivialization.

note_matches.heading: ### F6 — Cote 47, scan 7, admitted Lemma 2 and following support argument
note_matches.text: The attributed statement is explicitly present in Mumford (1970, §8(vii), p. 76): a nontrivial algebraically trivial line bundle on an abelian variety has vanishing cohomology in every degree. Together with base change, it removes the Poincaré direct image away from the zero section. It does not alone determine the scheme-theoretic structure along that section, the surviving cohomological degree, the determinant twist, or the specific comparison map constructed at the bottom of the page.

note_matches.heading: ### F7 — Cote 47, scan 8, first paragraph and unfinished verification
note_matches.text: **Editorial proof plan:** the direct image of the Poincaré line bundle is perfect, and the zero-section pushforward is perfect because that section is a regular immersion, so the cone of the proposed comparison is perfect. Vanishing of all its derived residue-field fibres then proves that the cone vanishes, by the local perfect-complex criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tags 0DJT and 0G99). The remaining task is to show that the particular map induces the required isomorphisms at the unit, not merely that the two sides have equal cohomology dimensions. **Confidence: high**, because the finite-complex criterion is established and isolates exactly the manuscript’s unfinished step.

note_matches.heading: ### F15 — Cote 47, scan 9, question about torsion
note_matches.text: A useful later comparison distinguishes a particular bundle’s integral Chern classes from an integral Fourier transform on the entire Chow group. Beckmann and de Gaay Fortman (2023, Theorem 3.8) characterize integral lifts of the Poincaré character using a specific one-cycle; under a symmetric ample principal polarization, they also relate this to preservation of Chow groups modulo torsion and to weak integral Fourier transforms. These additional hypotheses and the distinction between rational identities and integral lifts prevent the manuscript’s local heuristic from being treated as a general integral-transform theorem.

note_matches.heading: ### S8 — Endpoint calculations explain the revised operator formulas
note_matches.text: On a normalized string \(v_0,\ldots,v_r\), \(L\Lambda\) is identity except at \(v_0\), and \(\Lambda L\) is identity except at \(v_r\); their failures are therefore projectors onto opposite endpoints. This gives a direct way to check the draft's sums of \(p_i\), which are primitive-piece projections rather than the degree projectors \(\pi_i\). For a hyperplane section one must additionally test the evanescent middle summand, on which the relevant lowering operator vanishes. Such a check can expose an endpoint error in a proposed identity without promoting any of the visibly cancelled formulas back into the final argument.

note_matches.text: These post-freeze notes concern cote 47, scans 3–11; this file is undated, so the comparisons below make no claim of historical priority. Manuscript assertions, established literature, and editorial calculations are identified separately, and none changes the frozen transcription. In explanatory formulas only, write \(B=A^\vee\), \(g=n\), \(\pi_A:A\to S\), \(P\) for the Poincaré bundle rigidified along both zero sections, \(\omega_A=\det(\operatorname{Lie}A)^\vee\) on \(S\), and \(\tau_A=\omega_A^{-1}\); pullbacks of base classes are displayed or understood from their destination.

note_matches.heading: ### F4 — Cote 47, scan 5, inserted determinant factor; scans 6–7, Lemma 1
note_matches.text: Dualizing the Hodge-line identification gives \(\det\operatorname{Lie}A\simeq\det\operatorname{Lie}B\), without a principal polarization or an identification of the full Lie bundles. His Lemma 1.2.5 also identifies the Poincaré direct image with the zero-section pushforward of this inverse Hodge line, shifted by \(-g\); this preserves canonicity without choosing a trivialization.

note_matches.heading: ### F6 — Cote 47, scan 7, admitted Lemma 2 and following support argument
note_matches.text: The attributed statement is explicitly present in Mumford (1970, §8(vii), p. 76): a nontrivial algebraically trivial line bundle on an abelian variety has vanishing cohomology in every degree. Together with base change, it removes the Poincaré direct image away from the zero section. It does not alone determine the scheme-theoretic structure along that section, the surviving cohomological degree, the determinant twist, or the specific comparison map constructed at the bottom of the page.

note_matches.heading: ### F7 — Cote 47, scan 8, first paragraph and unfinished verification
note_matches.text: **Editorial proof plan:** the direct image of the Poincaré line bundle is perfect, and the zero-section pushforward is perfect because that section is a regular immersion, so the cone of the proposed comparison is perfect. Vanishing of all its derived residue-field fibres then proves that the cone vanishes, by the local perfect-complex criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tags 0DJT and 0G99). The remaining task is to show that the particular map induces the required isomorphisms at the unit, not merely that the two sides have equal cohomology dimensions. **Confidence: high**, because the finite-complex criterion is established and isolates exactly the manuscript’s unfinished step.

note_matches.heading: ### F15 — Cote 47, scan 9, question about torsion
note_matches.text: A useful later comparison distinguishes a particular bundle’s integral Chern classes from an integral Fourier transform on the entire Chow group. Beckmann and de Gaay Fortman (2023, Theorem 3.8) characterize integral lifts of the Poincaré character using a specific one-cycle; under a symmetric ample principal polarization, they also relate this to preservation of Chow groups modulo torsion and to weak integral Fourier transforms. These additional hypotheses and the distinction between rational identities and integral lifts prevent the manuscript’s local heuristic from being treated as a general integral-transform theorem.

note_matches.heading: ### R22 — Own idea: test the finite-fibre criterion without hidden flatness
note_matches.text: If this is read without further ambient hypotheses, let \(A=k[t]\) and \(B=A\times A/(t)\), with the diagonal \(A\)-algebra structure; then \(B\) is finite and its fibre at every maximal ideal is either \(k(\mathfrak m)\) or \(k(\mathfrak m)\times k(\mathfrak m)\), hence is finite étale. But \(B\simeq A\oplus A/(t)\) as an \(A\)-module is not flat, since multiplication by \(t\) kills a nonzero element, so \(B/A\) is not étale. Accordingly, the proposed equivalence needs the hypotheses of the referenced text to supply flatness or a condition that forces it; the counterexample does not decide whether those hypotheses were already in force. Using a product with the \(A\)-factor ensures that every fibre is nonempty, so this objection is not an artefact of allowing the zero algebra as an empty cover.

note_matches.heading: ## Fourier transforms, determinant lines, and Chern coefficients
note_matches.text: These post-freeze notes concern cote 47, scans 3–11; this file is undated, so the comparisons below make no claim of historical priority. Manuscript assertions, established literature, and editorial calculations are identified separately, and none changes the frozen transcription. In explanatory formulas only, write \(B=A^\vee\), \(g=n\), \(\pi_A:A\to S\), \(P\) for the Poincaré bundle rigidified along both zero sections, \(\omega_A=\det(\operatorname{Lie}A)^\vee\) on \(S\), and \(\tau_A=\omega_A^{-1}\); pullbacks of base classes are displayed or understood from their destination.

note_matches.heading: ### F4 — Cote 47, scan 5, inserted determinant factor; scans 6–7, Lemma 1
note_matches.text: Dualizing the Hodge-line identification gives \(\det\operatorname{Lie}A\simeq\det\operatorname{Lie}B\), without a principal polarization or an identification of the full Lie bundles. His Lemma 1.2.5 also identifies the Poincaré direct image with the zero-section pushforward of this inverse Hodge line, shifted by \(-g\); this preserves canonicity without choosing a trivialization.

note_matches.heading: ### F6 — Cote 47, scan 7, admitted Lemma 2 and following support argument
note_matches.text: The attributed statement is explicitly present in Mumford (1970, §8(vii), p. 76): a nontrivial algebraically trivial line bundle on an abelian variety has vanishing cohomology in every degree. Together with base change, it removes the Poincaré direct image away from the zero section. It does not alone determine the scheme-theoretic structure along that section, the surviving cohomological degree, the determinant twist, or the specific comparison map constructed at the bottom of the page.

note_matches.heading: ### F7 — Cote 47, scan 8, first paragraph and unfinished verification
note_matches.text: **Editorial proof plan:** the direct image of the Poincaré line bundle is perfect, and the zero-section pushforward is perfect because that section is a regular immersion, so the cone of the proposed comparison is perfect. Vanishing of all its derived residue-field fibres then proves that the cone vanishes, by the local perfect-complex criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tags 0DJT and 0G99). The remaining task is to show that the particular map induces the required isomorphisms at the unit, not merely that the two sides have equal cohomology dimensions. **Confidence: high**, because the finite-complex criterion is established and isolates exactly the manuscript’s unfinished step.

note_matches.heading: ### F15 — Cote 47, scan 9, question about torsion
note_matches.text: A useful later comparison distinguishes a particular bundle’s integral Chern classes from an integral Fourier transform on the entire Chow group. Beckmann and de Gaay Fortman (2023, Theorem 3.8) characterize integral lifts of the Poincaré character using a specific one-cycle; under a symmetric ample principal polarization, they also relate this to preservation of Chow groups modulo torsion and to weak integral Fourier transforms. These additional hypotheses and the distinction between rational identities and integral lifts prevent the manuscript’s local heuristic from being treated as a general integral-transform theorem.

note_matches.text: These post-freeze notes concern cote 47, scans 3–11; this file is undated, so the comparisons below make no claim of historical priority. Manuscript assertions, established literature, and editorial calculations are identified separately, and none changes the frozen transcription. In explanatory formulas only, write \(B=A^\vee\), \(g=n\), \(\pi_A:A\to S\), \(P\) for the Poincaré bundle rigidified along both zero sections, \(\omega_A=\det(\operatorname{Lie}A)^\vee\) on \(S\), and \(\tau_A=\omega_A^{-1}\); pullbacks of base classes are displayed or understood from their destination.

note_matches.heading: ### F4 — Cote 47, scan 5, inserted determinant factor; scans 6–7, Lemma 1
note_matches.text: Dualizing the Hodge-line identification gives \(\det\operatorname{Lie}A\simeq\det\operatorname{Lie}B\), without a principal polarization or an identification of the full Lie bundles. His Lemma 1.2.5 also identifies the Poincaré direct image with the zero-section pushforward of this inverse Hodge line, shifted by \(-g\); this preserves canonicity without choosing a trivialization.

note_matches.heading: ### F6 — Cote 47, scan 7, admitted Lemma 2 and following support argument
note_matches.text: The attributed statement is explicitly present in Mumford (1970, §8(vii), p. 76): a nontrivial algebraically trivial line bundle on an abelian variety has vanishing cohomology in every degree. Together with base change, it removes the Poincaré direct image away from the zero section. It does not alone determine the scheme-theoretic structure along that section, the surviving cohomological degree, the determinant twist, or the specific comparison map constructed at the bottom of the page.

note_matches.heading: ### F7 — Cote 47, scan 8, first paragraph and unfinished verification
note_matches.text: **Editorial proof plan:** the direct image of the Poincaré line bundle is perfect, and the zero-section pushforward is perfect because that section is a regular immersion, so the cone of the proposed comparison is perfect. Vanishing of all its derived residue-field fibres then proves that the cone vanishes, by the local perfect-complex criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tags 0DJT and 0G99). The remaining task is to show that the particular map induces the required isomorphisms at the unit, not merely that the two sides have equal cohomology dimensions. **Confidence: high**, because the finite-complex criterion is established and isolates exactly the manuscript’s unfinished step.

note_matches.heading: ### F15 — Cote 47, scan 9, question about torsion
note_matches.text: A useful later comparison distinguishes a particular bundle’s integral Chern classes from an integral Fourier transform on the entire Chow group. Beckmann and de Gaay Fortman (2023, Theorem 3.8) characterize integral lifts of the Poincaré character using a specific one-cycle; under a symmetric ample principal polarization, they also relate this to preservation of Chow groups modulo torsion and to weak integral Fourier transforms. These additional hypotheses and the distinction between rational identities and integral lifts prevent the manuscript’s local heuristic from being treated as a general integral-transform theorem.

note_matches.heading: ### S16 — A nilpotent kernel is not a zero kernel
note_matches.text: Under algebraicity of the Künneth components, Jannsen (1992, Corollary 1) identifies the kernel from homological to numerical degree-zero correspondence algebras with the Jacobson radical and proves it nilpotent. This isolates a precise obstruction to obtaining the draft's cohomological semisimplicity from numerical semisimplicity. Nilpotence alone permits a nonzero ideal, so it is not a proof that the two equivalence relations coincide; an additional positivity or equivalence argument must annihilate that kernel. The distinction also prevents treating a numerical projector as a canonical cohomological projector solely because some lift exists.

note_matches.heading: ### S17 — Finite-field Künneth projectors illustrate a narrower later result
note_matches.text: ### S17 — Finite-field Künneth projectors illustrate a narrower later result

note_matches.heading: ### S17 — Finite-field Künneth projectors illustrate a narrower later result
note_matches.text: For smooth projective varieties over finite fields, Katz and Messing (1974, Theorem 2) construct rational algebraic Künneth projectors as rational combinations of graphs of Frobenius iterates, compatibly with the cohomology theories in their hypotheses. Their theorem also gives integral, theory-independent characteristic polynomials for integral degree-zero correspondences. These results strengthen two particular ingredients appearing in the letters, but the projector statement is published condition \(C\), not the draft's stronger inverse-operator condition \(C_\ell\). Moreover, rationality in the Cayley–Hamilton criterion still has to be coupled with the required algebraic complementary-degree isomorphisms.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The claim is that a subring containing every graded projector inherits the homogeneous decomposition of the endomorphism ring. A proof has to use the finiteness of the grading to ensure that the displayed sums remain algebraic sums inside the subring, and then check multiplication of the components.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:3 — reading question
note_matches.text: The small insertion specifying which module underlies the endomorphism ring is difficult to resolve, and the square bracket opened in the main paragraph has no confidently identified closing partner on this sheet. The correction from algebra language to subring language should be retained as a revision rather than silently harmonised.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:5:1 — reading question
note_matches.text: The finite support is now tied to a prescribed even interval; the small parenthesis is read as “pair” with some residual doubt. This added symmetry matters for the reconstruction pairing i with 2n−i.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:6:4 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: A single invertible map in the relevant homogeneous block implies both joint kernel and image conditions. This is the immediate route from a Lefschetz-type isomorphism to uniqueness of the grading projectors; the continuation must be read before assigning its full scope.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:7:3 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: A degree-two element is introduced as a structured source for the preceding homogeneous isomorphisms. The continuation should identify its power and range conditions; no Lefschetz axiom is inserted into the transcription in advance.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:9:1 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: The Lefschetz-type isomorphisms are used to infer uniqueness of the grading projectors before the existence of their inverses inside the chosen subring is assumed. The distinction between uniqueness under (6.1) and descent/existence under the strengthened (6.2) should be kept explicit.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:9:4 — own idea
note_matches.text: **Location:** cote 16, scan 9, projection notation at foot.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:11:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The proof of primitive-projector membership starts an induction on the outside of the interval [i,2n−i], then adds both boundary degrees. The inserted direction is visually less secure than the interval and should be settled from the ink before giving a formally ordered proof.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:12:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: **Location:** cote 16, scan 12, opening action and first isomorphism.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:12:2 — reading question
note_matches.text: **Location:** cote 16, scan 12, isomorphism preceding (6.9).

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:5 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Independence of the symplectic model is claimed from the multiplication rules. A proof should distinguish an abstract algebra determined up to isomorphism from a canonically identified algebra, and make clear whether the independence assertion still holds under the arbitrary-ring extension in the margin.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:6 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The proposition begins an equivalence between the Lefschetz condition with Λ in E and the existence of a graded-algebra homomorphism from Φ₀ to E. The arrow’s required value on generators and any uniqueness clause continue onto the next page and are essential to the precise statement.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:7 — own idea
note_matches.text: Once the indices are fixed from the manuscript, calculate the rank of the proposed matrix algebra and compare it with the rank of the operator algebra acting on the integral exterior model for n=1 and n=2. A discrepancy would localise a failure of the basis claim, a range error, or the normalisation issue already visible on scan14.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:16:1 — reading question
note_matches.text: The added requirement that the homomorphism carry the model projectors to the given π_i is explicitly labelled essential. A formulation retaining only the prescribed image of L would omit a hypothesis the author took care to add.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The corollary asserts uniqueness of the homomorphism subject to preservation of both L and the grading projectors. The result depends on the preceding proposition and on the uniqueness of the projector family from the graded ring; the added integer 2n≥0 supplies an explicit parameter for that assertion.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:4:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Orthogonal idempotents summing to one are asserted to induce the required homogeneous decomposition. The subsequent block decomposition supplies a proof strategy; the marginal extension from ℤ to an arbitrary group would require careful attention to the order of multiplication for a noncommutative grading group.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:9:2 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The pair of module conditions is recast as ring identities involving L and homogeneous inverses w_i. The equivalence requires restriction to the indicated graded summands and extension of the inverse by the projectors; the manuscript makes the availability of those projectors part of the intrinsic formulation.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:5 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Independence of the symplectic model is claimed from the multiplication rules. A proof should distinguish an abstract algebra determined up to isomorphism from a canonically identified algebra, and make clear whether the independence assertion still holds under the arbitrary-ring extension in the margin.

Its hypotheses begin on an absent preceding typescript page; the extension and rational-point descriptions must be interpreted with that limitation.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:25:2 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The sheet separates the Lefschetz condition into nondegeneracy of the alternating form and Poincaré duality into nondegeneracy of the symmetric form. One should verify the stated equivalences directly on the complete multiplication table, keeping the normalization of ξ² and the dual-space pairing fixed.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:25:4 — own idea
note_matches.text: Treat the boxed relation as polynomial equations on the triple (φ,ψ,Q), then examine the locus where both forms are nondegenerate under changes of bases of V and W. Low-dimensional examples could separate purely graded Poincaré–Lefschetz algebras from algebras satisfying additional Hodge positivity conditions.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:26:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The replacement passage asserts extension of a generic Cartan subgroup after shrinking the base, with the extension chosen inside H. Checking the argument requires the precise hypotheses on the group schemes and the base; this errata page itself does not supply them.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:27:4 — own idea
note_matches.text: The reformulation suggests classifying extensions of the symmetric bilinear form induced by a four-form, together with a norm-one vector whose contraction gives a nondegenerate alternating form. Testing this construction in dimensions two and four may give explicit moduli and clarify when the special case χ=0 remains compatible with duality.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:30:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Acyclicity is stated for the Amitsur-type complex of positive-degree multiplicative-group cohomology under a purely inseparable field extension. The proof is not on this sheet; checking it requires the cohomology topology, the hypotheses of Th.6, and the results cited as [5,21].

note_matches.heading: ## 16:35:2 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The introduction announces an extension of the Grothendieck group to integer degrees related to Bott periodicity. This page contains only the beginning of the Banach-category definition; the precise additional structure and axioms must be checked against the continuation rather than supplied here.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The claim is that a subring containing every graded projector inherits the homogeneous decomposition of the endomorphism ring. A proof has to use the finiteness of the grading to ensure that the displayed sums remain algebraic sums inside the subring, and then check multiplication of the components.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:3 — reading question
note_matches.text: The small insertion specifying which module underlies the endomorphism ring is difficult to resolve, and the square bracket opened in the main paragraph has no confidently identified closing partner on this sheet. The correction from algebra language to subring language should be retained as a revision rather than silently harmonised.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:6:4 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: A single invertible map in the relevant homogeneous block implies both joint kernel and image conditions. This is the immediate route from a Lefschetz-type isomorphism to uniqueness of the grading projectors; the continuation must be read before assigning its full scope.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:7:3 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: A degree-two element is introduced as a structured source for the preceding homogeneous isomorphisms. The continuation should identify its power and range conditions; no Lefschetz axiom is inserted into the transcription in advance.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:9:1 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: The Lefschetz-type isomorphisms are used to infer uniqueness of the grading projectors before the existence of their inverses inside the chosen subring is assumed. The distinction between uniqueness under (6.1) and descent/existence under the strengthened (6.2) should be kept explicit.

note_matches.text: Independence of the symplectic model is claimed from the multiplication rules. note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:6 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The proposition begins an equivalence between the Lefschetz condition with Λ in E and the existence of a graded-algebra homomorphism from Φ₀ to E. The arrow’s required value on generators and any uniqueness clause continue onto the next page and are essential to the precise statement.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:16:1 — reading question
note_matches.text: The added requirement that the homomorphism carry the model projectors to the given π_i is explicitly labelled essential. A formulation retaining only the prescribed image of L would omit a hypothesis the author took care to add.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The corollary asserts uniqueness of the homomorphism subject to preservation of both L and the grading projectors. The result depends on the preceding proposition and on the uniqueness of the projector family from the graded ring; the added integer 2n≥0 supplies an explicit parameter for that assertion.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:4 — conjecture
note_matches.text: The author asks whether the image of L alone determines at most one homomorphism, then answers negatively on the same page. The n=1 example and the final sentence explicitly insist that L and the π_i must be prescribed together; this should not be catalogued as a question left unanswered by the manuscript.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:5 — own idea
note_matches.text: Turn the author’s negative example into an explicit pair of homomorphisms by conjugating inside the two-dimensional Lefschetz block by 1+tL. When L²=0 this element has inverse 1−tL, fixes L by conjugation, and can move Λ and the endpoint projectors, giving a concrete test of the failure of uniqueness.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:20:5 — reading question
note_matches.text: The lower-right calculation introduces barred generators and multiplication relations. Whether the second bar on the final right-hand side is intentional is a paleographical question; mathematical simplification would erase the distinction being tested.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:22:3 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: The author asks whether finite projectivity over A can yield a converse, then immediately records failure for an endomorphism algebra of a graded module in degrees0 through4. This is an exploratory question accompanied by a negative observation, not a theorem proved in this paragraph.

note_matches.heading: ## Fourier transforms, determinant lines, and Chern coefficients
note_matches.text: These post-freeze notes concern cote 47, scans 3–11; this file is undated, so the comparisons below make no claim of historical priority. Manuscript assertions, established literature, and editorial calculations are identified separately, and none changes the frozen transcription. In explanatory formulas only, write \(B=A^\vee\), \(g=n\), \(\pi_A:A\to S\), \(P\) for the Poincaré bundle rigidified along both zero sections, \(\omega_A=\det(\operatorname{Lie}A)^\vee\) on \(S\), and \(\tau_A=\omega_A^{-1}\); pullbacks of base classes are displayed or understood from their destination.

note_matches.heading: ### F4 — Cote 47, scan 5, inserted determinant factor; scans 6–7, Lemma 1
note_matches.text: Dualizing the Hodge-line identification gives \(\det\operatorname{Lie}A\simeq\det\operatorname{Lie}B\), without a principal polarization or an identification of the full Lie bundles. His Lemma 1.2.5 also identifies the Poincaré direct image with the zero-section pushforward of this inverse Hodge line, shifted by \(-g\); this preserves canonicity without choosing a trivialization.

note_matches.heading: ### F6 — Cote 47, scan 7, admitted Lemma 2 and following support argument
note_matches.text: The attributed statement is explicitly present in Mumford (1970, §8(vii), p. 76): a nontrivial algebraically trivial line bundle on an abelian variety has vanishing cohomology in every degree. Together with base change, it removes the Poincaré direct image away from the zero section. It does not alone determine the scheme-theoretic structure along that section, the surviving cohomological degree, the determinant twist, or the specific comparison map constructed at the bottom of the page.

note_matches.heading: ### F7 — Cote 47, scan 8, first paragraph and unfinished verification
note_matches.text: **Editorial proof plan:** the direct image of the Poincaré line bundle is perfect, and the zero-section pushforward is perfect because that section is a regular immersion, so the cone of the proposed comparison is perfect. Vanishing of all its derived residue-field fibres then proves that the cone vanishes, by the local perfect-complex criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tags 0DJT and 0G99). The remaining task is to show that the particular map induces the required isomorphisms at the unit, not merely that the two sides have equal cohomology dimensions. **Confidence: high**, because the finite-complex criterion is established and isolates exactly the manuscript’s unfinished step.

note_matches.heading: ### F15 — Cote 47, scan 9, question about torsion
note_matches.text: A useful later comparison distinguishes a particular bundle’s integral Chern classes from an integral Fourier transform on the entire Chow group. Beckmann and de Gaay Fortman (2023, Theorem 3.8) characterize integral lifts of the Poincaré character using a specific one-cycle; under a symmetric ample principal polarization, they also relate this to preservation of Chow groups modulo torsion and to weak integral Fourier transforms. These additional hypotheses and the distinction between rational identities and integral lifts prevent the manuscript’s local heuristic from being treated as a general integral-transform theorem.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:4:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Orthogonal idempotents summing to one are asserted to induce the required homogeneous decomposition. The subsequent block decomposition supplies a proof strategy; the marginal extension from ℤ to an arbitrary group would require careful attention to the order of multiplication for a noncommutative grading group.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:9:2 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The pair of module conditions is recast as ring identities involving L and homogeneous inverses w_i. The equivalence requires restriction to the indicated graded summands and extension of the inverse by the projectors; the manuscript makes the availability of those projectors part of the intrinsic formulation.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:5 — unproved claim

A proof should distinguish an abstract algebra determined up to isomorphism from a canonically identified algebra, and make clear whether the independence assertion still holds under the arbitrary-ring extension in the margin.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:25:4 — own idea
note_matches.text: Treat the boxed relation as polynomial equations on the triple (φ,ψ,Q), then examine the locus where both forms are nondegenerate under changes of bases of V and W. Low-dimensional examples could separate purely graded Poincaré–Lefschetz algebras from algebras satisfying additional Hodge positivity conditions.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:26:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The replacement passage asserts extension of a generic Cartan subgroup after shrinking the base, with the extension chosen inside H. Checking the argument requires the precise hypotheses on the group schemes and the base; this errata page itself does not supply them.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:27:4 — own idea
note_matches.text: The reformulation suggests classifying extensions of the symmetric bilinear form induced by a four-form, together with a norm-one vector whose contraction gives a nondegenerate alternating form. Testing this construction in dimensions two and four may give explicit moduli and clarify when the special case χ=0 remains compatible with duality.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:30:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Acyclicity is stated for the Amitsur-type complex of positive-degree multiplicative-group cohomology under a purely inseparable field extension. The proof is not on this sheet; checking it requires the cohomology topology, the hypotheses of Th.6, and the results cited as [5,21].

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The claim is that a subring containing every graded projector inherits the homogeneous decomposition of the endomorphism ring. A proof has to use the finiteness of the grading to ensure that the displayed sums remain algebraic sums inside the subring, and then check multiplication of the components.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:3:3 — reading question
note_matches.text: The small insertion specifying which module underlies the endomorphism ring is difficult to resolve, and the square bracket opened in the main paragraph has no confidently identified closing partner on this sheet. The correction from algebra language to subring language should be retained as a revision rather than silently harmonised.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:6:4 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: A single invertible map in the relevant homogeneous block implies both joint kernel and image conditions. This is the immediate route from a Lefschetz-type isomorphism to uniqueness of the grading projectors; the continuation must be read before assigning its full scope.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:7:3 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: A degree-two element is introduced as a structured source for the preceding homogeneous isomorphisms. The continuation should identify its power and range conditions; no Lefschetz axiom is inserted into the transcription in advance.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:9:1 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: The Lefschetz-type isomorphisms are used to infer uniqueness of the grading projectors before the existence of their inverses inside the chosen subring is assumed. The distinction between uniqueness under (6.1) and descent/existence under the strengthened (6.2) should be kept explicit.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:12:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: **Location:** cote 16, scan 12, opening action and first isomorphism.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:12:2 — reading question
note_matches.text: **Location:** cote 16, scan 12, isomorphism preceding (6.9).

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:5 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: Independence of the symplectic model is claimed from the multiplication rules. A proof should distinguish an abstract algebra determined up to isomorphism from a canonically identified algebra, and make clear whether the independence assertion still holds under the arbitrary-ring extension in the margin.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:15:6 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The proposition begins an equivalence between the Lefschetz condition with Λ in E and the existence of a graded-algebra homomorphism from Φ₀ to E. The arrow’s required value on generators and any uniqueness clause continue onto the next page and are essential to the precise statement.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:16:1 — reading question
note_matches.text: The added requirement that the homomorphism carry the model projectors to the given π_i is explicitly labelled essential. A formulation retaining only the prescribed image of L would omit a hypothesis the author took care to add.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:1 — unproved claim
note_matches.text: The corollary asserts uniqueness of the homomorphism subject to preservation of both L and the grading projectors. The result depends on the preceding proposition and on the uniqueness of the projector family from the graded ring; the added integer 2n≥0 supplies an explicit parameter for that assertion.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:4 — conjecture
note_matches.text: The author asks whether the image of L alone determines at most one homomorphism, then answers negatively on the same page. The n=1 example and the final sentence explicitly insist that L and the π_i must be prescribed together; this should not be catalogued as a question left unanswered by the manuscript.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:17:5 — own idea
note_matches.text: Turn the author’s negative example into an explicit pair of homomorphisms by conjugating inside the two-dimensional Lefschetz block by 1+tL. When L²=0 this element has inverse 1−tL, fixes L by conjugation, and can move Λ and the endpoint projectors, giving a concrete test of the failure of uniqueness.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:20:5 — reading question
note_matches.text: The lower-right calculation introduces barred generators and multiplication relations. Whether the second bar on the final right-hand side is intentional is a paleographical question; mathematical simplification would erase the distinction being tested.

note_matches.heading: ## 16:22:3 — unpursued implication
note_matches.text: The author asks whether finite projectivity over A can yield a converse, then immediately records failure for an endomorphism algebra of a graded module in degrees0 through4. This is an exploratory question accompanied by a negative observation, not a theorem proved in this paragraph.
